question: How do pressure-only Reynolds and mass-conserving JFO predictions compare with Gangrade et al. and with extended load and fixed-eccentricity sensitivities when 0.5 MPa is only a scale and the 4 mm replenishment port is held at ambient pressure?

source_artifacts.path: ../../docs/papers_sorted/conical-journal-bearing/cfd/Performance Analysis of a Conical Hydrodynamic Journal Bearing.pdf

expected_outputs.role: separate Reynolds and JFO load equilibria
four load-equilibrium-seeded and eleven prescribed-eccentricity 3D single-phase diagnostics
per-case pressure, flow, load, mesh, and convergence evidence
separate Reynolds/JFO fixed-position sweep from eccentricity ratio 0.40 through 0.90 by 0.05
compact static, dynamic, and stability coefficients

limitations: The paper's 0.5 MPa value is used only as a nondimensional reference; no 0.5 MPa gauge feed is imposed.
The retained 4 mm ambient replenishment patch comes from the project geometry. The paper identifies rig port IP1 but does not disclose its diameter or include it in the published FEM mesh.
Figure values are manual graph reads and do not replace source data supplied by the authors.
Figure 8 does not disclose the plotted zero-angle mapping to the local coordinates; any fitted circular phase is a diagnostic alignment, not predictive validation.
The 5 MPa Babbitt pressure ceiling is a provisional supervisor-supplied design gate, not a paper value or numerical gate.
The 3D runs are single-phase Navier-Stokes diagnostics at fixed geometry. Reynolds and JFO label the 2D seed position; neither boundary condition is imposed on the 3D volume solve.

Each prescribed eccentricity has one 3D case because Reynolds and JFO do not define different geometry at fixed position; duplicating the single-phase volume solve by 2D model label would be identical.

The stiffness coefficients use two central-difference amplitudes. Damping uses a frozen-cavity instantaneous linearization because the paper does not disclose perturbation amplitude or moving rupture-boundary details.
The three declared surface grids test feed-patch discretization sensitivity and are not presented as a formal grid-convergence-index sequence.
Eccentricity ratios between and beyond the paper's plotted points are a separate fixed-position sensitivity; they are not attributed to the paper.
